title: Why only 100 positions?
summary: The context window, and why it is a hard limit.

steps.text: The position table has exactly 100 rows, so the model can only ever see 100 positions. Longer text is cut to its last 100 {{units}}: the window **slides**.
steps.prompt: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her dog Max. One day, they went to the park and saw a big tree.

bpe.prompt: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her dog Max. One day, they went to the park and saw a big tree. Lily wanted to climb the tree, but it was very tall. Max barked and ran around the tree. A kind old man saw them and smiled. He helped Lily climb up to the first branch. From the branch, Lily could see the whole park. She saw her mom waving at her. Lily waved back and laughed. Then she climbed down and gave Max a big hug. They walked home together, happy and tired.

steps.text: Under the prompt box: the {{units}} that slid out of view are no longer anywhere in the network. Whatever they said is forgotten unless it was repeated later.

Generation repeats this for every new {{unit}}: run the whole window, read the last row, sample, append, slide. The attention matrix is T×T, so cost grows with the square of the window: one reason context is limited.
